Distance Development wrote:

> > Hi Rick,
> >
> > I'm sending this one to the list in case others are interested in the data
> > formats used by the distance analysis engine, especially the commands to tell
> > the D3.5 engine about the flat-file format.
> >
> > My answers are interspersed among your questions.
> >
> > Cheers,
> >
> > - Len
> >
> > On Tue, 4 Jan 2000 20:24:34 -0000, Rick Woodburn wrote:
> >
>> > >Dear Len
>> > >
>> > >I have made good progress in using the analysis engine as a stand alone
>> > >program, using the input file. However, I am having problems working out the
>> > >syntax for the infile command.
>> > >
>> > >I have written a program to produce both hierarchical and flat formats.
>> > >Could you tell me the syntax to import each of the formats?
>> > >
>> > >My files look like this (same data shown):
>> > >
>> > >Hierarchical:
>> > >
>> > >stratum /label=EC71 ;
>> > >sample /effort=1.2 /label=NY0922 ;
>> > >0 0 0 ;
>> > >sample /effort=0.4 /label=NY5381 ;
>> > >0 0 0 ;
>> > >sample /effort=1.2 /label=NY5882 ;
>> > >0 0 0 ;
>> > >sample /effort=0.4 /label=NZ1064 ;
>> > >1 0 0 ;
>> > >sample /effort=0.4 /label=NZ1364 ;
>> > >6 2 0 ;
>> > >sample /effort=0.8 /label=NZ2681 ;
>> > >8 3 4 ;
>> > >stratum /label=EC72 ;
>> > >sample /effort=0.4 /label=SD9085 ;
>> > >0 0 0 ;
>> > >sample /effort=0.4 /label=SE0051 ;
>> > >1 2 0 ;
>> > >
>> > >
>> > >Flat:
>> > >
>> > >EC71;NY0922;1.2;b1;
>> > >EC71;NY5381;0.4;b1;
>> > >EC71;NY5882;1.2;b1;
>> > >EC71;NZ1064;0.4;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;62.5
>> > >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;62.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;62.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;62.5
>> > >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;62.5
>> > >EC72;SD9085;0.4;b1;
>> > >EC72;SE0051;0.4;b1;12.5
>> > >EC72;SE0051;0.4;b1;62.5
>> > >EC72;SE0051;0.4;b1;62.5
>> > >
>> > >
>> > >Where, for example;
>> > >EC72 is the region,
>> > >SE0051 is the sample,
>> > >0.4 is the effort (line length),
>> > >b1 is the habitat type (originally included for post-strat analysis)
>> > >62.5 is the midpoint in the distance group 25-100m.
>> > >
>> > >For the Hierarchical format I have used:
>> > >
>> > > Data;
>> > > Infile=XXXX.dat;
>> > > End;
>> > >
>> > > With these commands, Distance recognises the strata and calculates the
>> > >total effort correctly, but makes some mistakes with recognising
>> > >observations, throwing the whole calculation.
> >
> > I am not aware of any problems with the distance analysis engine recognizing
> > the hierarchical format, although this is only used the Distance 3.5 engine
> > when importing old D2.2 command files. Remember that you need to tell
> > Distance that your data are in groups with the command
> >
> > DISTANCE=PERP/INTERVALS=0, 25, 100, 250;
> >
> > (assuming these are the right cutpoints) in the OPTIONS section (and
> > therefore you don't need to use /INTERVALS in the DISTANCE command in the
> > ESTIMATE section). The Distance command language takes a bit of getting used
> > to, I'm afraid (which is why we wrote the windows interface). It's unlikely
> > that you'll be able to simply cut and paste from the Log section of the
> > interface without understanding what you're doing and get good results. If
> > you are not sure, I suggest you download Distance 2.2 from the web site, and
> > the documentation file (a separate download) - then have a look at the D2.2
> > example files, and then try your command file under D2.2 to check it works
> > there.
> >
>> > >For the Flat format I have used;
>> > >
>> > > Data; /Structure=Flat;
>> > > Infile=XXXX.dat;
>> > > End;
>> > >
>> > > I assume that this does not work because the program needs to be told the
>> > >variable labels. Also is a declaration of the delimiter needed?
> >
> > For one thing, I think it will not work as you have a semicolon directly
> > after the Data command, which you don't need.
> >
> > For another, you won't be able to import the "habitat field" that you have in
> > your data file - post-stratification is done by the D3.5 interface, not the
> > analysis engine.
> >
> > Thirdly, your data needs to be Tab delimited, as the engine doesn't recognize
> > any other format. (It's the interface that can cope with comma delimited,
> > etc).
> >
> > Below, I have included some information that Jeff Laake wrote about the flat
> > data structure and was included in the Distance 3.0 readme file (Distance 3.0
> > was the first version to use the flat file structure). Note that unlike the
> > heirarchical data, you will have to enter the data as ungrouped and then
> > analyze it as grouped (using the /INTERVALS switch in the DISTANCE command
> > under ESTIMATE). Hopefully this will answer your flat format questions. If
> > not, let me know.
> >
> > Good luck!
> >
> > Abstract from Jeff's readme file:
> > ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
> > New Data Structure
> > A new method of data entry has been added to v3.0. The standard
> > hierarchical data structure in early versions is still accepted but a flat
> > file data structure has been added. A /Structure switch has been added to
> > the Data command which takes the values Flat or Hierarchy (default). Flat
> > file data entry enables easy access to data that are kept in spreadsheets or
> > databases by exporting the data into a file with tab-delimited fields. There
> > are 3 steps to using the flat file data structure:
> > 1) Create a file with the data fields delimited by tabs (most easily done
> > with a spreadsheet or database),
> > 2) Specify to DISTANCE the order of the data fields, using the FIELDS command
> > unless you have used the default order, and
> > 3) Specify to DISTANCE the name of the file containing the data, using the
> > INFILE command (keyboard entry is not allowed).
> > The flat file data structure is limited to entering ungrouped data, but
> > grouped data can be entered ungrouped and analyzed as grouped.
> >
> > Creating the data file
> > Create a data file which has a record (line) for each observation (sighting)
> > and a record for any sample (line or point) without any observations. Each
> > record should contain the following fields separated by tabs:
> > a) Distance data
> > DISTANCE if TYPE=LINE and DIST=PERP
> > DISTANCE if TYPE=POINT or CUE
> > DISTANCE & ANGLE if TYPE=LINE and DIST=RADIAL
> > b) Cluster size
> > SIZE if OBJECT=CLUSTER
> > c) Sample data
> > SMP_LABEL required (up to 50 characters)
> > SMP_EFFORT required(except for default value of 1)
> > d) Stratum data (optional)
> > STR_LABEL optional (up to 50 characters)
> > STR_AREA optional size of geographic region
> > to compute abundance
> >
> > If there are no observations for a sample, the distance and cluster size data
> > should be left blank and only the sample/strata data given. The records in
> > the file should be grouped by sample and stratum (if used) but they do not
> > need to be sorted by the label. For example,
> >
> > Stratum Sample Distance
> > ------- ---------- --------
> > Str1 10 Sample1 1 10.3
> > Str1 10 Sample2 1 - no observation for this sample
> > Str2 10 Sample3 1 1.1
> > Str2 10 Sample4 1 5.5
> > Str2 10 Sample4 1 53.4
> >
> > The following ordering would incorrectly create 3 strata:
> > Stratum Sample Distance
> > ------- ---------- --------
> > Str1 10 Sample1 1 10.3
> > Str2 10 Sample3 1 1.1
> > Str2 10 Sample4 1 5.5
> > Str2 10 Sample4 1 53.4
> > Str1 10 Sample2 1 - no observation for this sample
> >
> > Sample and stratum data only need to be given on the first record identifying
> > the stratum or sample. The correct example above could be given as:
> >
> > Stratum Sample Distance
> > ------- ---------- --------
> > Str1 10 Sample1 1 10.3
> > Sample2 1 - no observation for this sample
> > Str2 10 Sample3 1 1.1
> > Sample4 1 5.5
> > 53.4
> >
> > Empty fields are indicated by adjoining tabs delimiting an empty field. With
> > database software, an outer join between and sample and observation tables
> > will create the appropriate file structure. An outer join will create a
> > record for samples with no observations.
> >
> > Specifying the order of the fields: The order of the fields within the
> > record can follow the default order of (STR_LABEL, STR_AREA, SMP_LABEL,
> > SMP_EFFORT, DISTANCE, ANGLE, SIZE) in which ANGLE and SIZE are only needed
> > under the appropriate conditions or the order can be specified to DISTANCE
> > with the FIELDS command. The FIELDS command has the following syntax:
> >
> > FIELDS = fieldname1, fieldname2, ... ;
> >
> > where the fieldnames are from the following list and the order within the
> > list should match the order within the record:
> >
> > STR_LABEL, STR_AREA, SMP_LABEL, SMP_EFFORT, DISTANCE, ANGLE, SIZE
> >
> > Specifying the input filename: The data filename is specified with the INFILE
> > command which has the following syntax:
> >
> > INFILE = filename;
> >
> > ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
> >
>> > >
>> > >Thanks for any help that you can give.
>> > >Happy Y2K.
>> > >
>> > >Rick
>> > >
>> > >
>> > >
> >
> > --
> > Len Thomas, Co-ordinator
> > Distance Development Project
> > Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
> > Mathematical Institute, University of St Andrews
> > Scotland KY16 9SS
> >
> > email: dist...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk
> > RUWPA home page: http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk
> > Distance home page: http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/

messages.subject: ANSWER: D3.5 analysis engine data formats
parts:
Hi Rick,

I'm sending this one to the list in case others are interested in the data
formats used by the distance analysis engine, especially the commands to tell
the D3.5 engine about the flat-file format.

My answers are interspersed among your questions.

Cheers,

- Len

On Tue, 4 Jan 2000 20:24:34 -0000, Rick Woodburn wrote:

> >Dear Len
> >
> >I have made good progress in using the analysis engine as a stand alone
> >program, using the input file. However, I am having problems working out the
> >syntax for the infile command.
> >
> >I have written a program to produce both hierarchical and flat formats.
> >Could you tell me the syntax to import each of the formats?
> >
> >My files look like this (same data shown):
> >
> >Hierarchical:
> >
> >stratum /label=EC71 ;
> >sample /effort=1.2 /label=NY0922 ;
> >0 0 0 ;
> >sample /effort=0.4 /label=NY5381 ;
> >0 0 0 ;
> >sample /effort=1.2 /label=NY5882 ;
> >0 0 0 ;
> >sample /effort=0.4 /label=NZ1064 ;
> >1 0 0 ;
> >sample /effort=0.4 /label=NZ1364 ;
> >6 2 0 ;
> >sample /effort=0.8 /label=NZ2681 ;
> >8 3 4 ;
> >stratum /label=EC72 ;
> >sample /effort=0.4 /label=SD9085 ;
> >0 0 0 ;
> >sample /effort=0.4 /label=SE0051 ;
> >1 2 0 ;
> >
> >
> >Flat:
> >
> >EC71;NY0922;1.2;b1;
> >EC71;NY5381;0.4;b1;
> >EC71;NY5882;1.2;b1;
> >EC71;NZ1064;0.4;b1;12.5
> >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;12.5

> >EC71;NZ1364;0.4;b1;62.5
> >EC71;NZ2681;0.8;b1;12.5

Abstract from Jeff's readme file:
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
New Data Structure
A new method of data entry has been added to v3.0. The standard
hierarchical data structure in early versions is still accepted but a flat
file data structure has been added. A /Structure switch has been added to
the Data command which takes the values Flat or Hierarchy (default). Flat
file data entry enables easy access to data that are kept in spreadsheets or
databases by exporting the data into a file with tab-delimited fields. There
are 3 steps to using the flat file data structure:
1) Create a file with the data fields delimited by tabs (most easily done
with a spreadsheet or database),
2) Specify to DISTANCE the order of the data fields, using the FIELDS command
unless you have used the default order, and
3) Specify to DISTANCE the name of the file containing the data, using the
INFILE command (keyboard entry is not allowed).
The flat file data structure is limited to entering ungrouped data, but
grouped data can be entered ungrouped and analyzed as grouped.

Creating the data file
Create a data file which has a record (line) for each observation (sighting)
and a record for any sample (line or point) without any observations. Each
record should contain the following fields separated by tabs:
a) Distance data
DISTANCE if TYPE=LINE and DIST=PERP
DISTANCE if TYPE=POINT or CUE
DISTANCE & ANGLE if TYPE=LINE and DIST=RADIAL
b) Cluster size
SIZE if OBJECT=CLUSTER
c) Sample data
SMP_LABEL required (up to 50 characters)
SMP_EFFORT required(except for default value of 1)
d) Stratum data (optional)
STR_LABEL optional (up to 50 characters)
STR_AREA optional size of geographic region
to compute abundance

If there are no observations for a sample, the distance and cluster size data
should be left blank and only the sample/strata data given. The records in
the file should be grouped by sample and stratum (if used) but they do not
need to be sorted by the label. For example,

Stratum Sample Distance
------- ---------- --------
Str1 10 Sample1 1 10.3
Str1 10 Sample2 1 - no observation for this sample
Str2 10 Sample3 1 1.1
Str2 10 Sample4 1 5.5
Str2 10 Sample4 1 53.4

The following ordering would incorrectly create 3 strata:
Stratum Sample Distance
------- ---------- --------
Str1 10 Sample1 1 10.3
Str2 10 Sample3 1 1.1
Str2 10 Sample4 1 5.5
Str2 10 Sample4 1 53.4
Str1 10 Sample2 1 - no observation for this sample

Sample and stratum data only need to be given on the first record identifying
the stratum or sample. The correct example above could be given as:

Stratum Sample Distance
------- ---------- --------
Str1 10 Sample1 1 10.3
Sample2 1 - no observation for this sample
Str2 10 Sample3 1 1.1
Sample4 1 5.5
53.4

Empty fields are indicated by adjoining tabs delimiting an empty field. With
database software, an outer join between and sample and observation tables
will create the appropriate file structure. An outer join will create a
record for samples with no observations.

Specifying the order of the fields: The order of the fields within the
record can follow the default order of (STR_LABEL, STR_AREA, SMP_LABEL,
SMP_EFFORT, DISTANCE, ANGLE, SIZE) in which ANGLE and SIZE are only needed
under the appropriate conditions or the order can be specified to DISTANCE
with the FIELDS command. The FIELDS command has the following syntax:

FIELDS = fieldname1, fieldname2, ... ;

where the fieldnames are from the following list and the order within the
list should match the order within the record:

STR_LABEL, STR_AREA, SMP_LABEL, SMP_EFFORT, DISTANCE, ANGLE, SIZE

Specifying the input filename: The data filename is specified with the INFILE
command which has the following syntax:

INFILE = filename;
